title: Tenant-aware feature switch integration cookbook
author: Celeste Ramirez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This cookbook documents recommended integration patterns for tenant-scoped feature switches across Redwood's platform. It combines design patterns, schema examples, telemetry and dashboard recipes, runbook steps for safe rollouts, automated rollback criteria, and a short retrospective template for post-rollout review. This is intended for platform engineers, operator teams, and product owners coordinating multi-tenant rollouts.

When to use this guide
- New features that may impact latency, token cost, or model quality per tenant.
- Behavioural changes (prompt templates, reranking heuristics) that must be gated by tenant.
- Experiments requiring controlled exposure, KPI gating, or immediate rollback capability.

Key goals
- Minimize blast radius per-tenant.
- Provide clear observability and automated safety gates.
- Make rollouts repeatable and auditable.

Design patterns and tradeoffs
1) Scope choices
   - Global switch (global): Fast and simple, but high blast radius. Use only for non-risky UX flags.
   - Tenant-scoped switch (tenant): Defaults to off. Stores per-tenant metadata and rollout percent. Good for production experiments.
   - Cohort-based switch (cohort): Group tenants by risk profile (e.g., dev, low-volume, enterprise) and apply policies.

2) Rollout strategies
   - Fixed-percent progressive rollout: Increase percent of tenant traffic in steps (1%, 5%, 20%, 100%) with evaluation windows.
   - Tenant whitelist: Start with specific tenant IDs (customer X, internal staging) before percent ramp.
   - Metric-gated rollout (KPI gating): Only advance when SLOs/quality metrics meet thresholds.

3) Safety primitives (must-haves)
   - Kill switch: Immediate global-off with a single API call.
   - Tenant-level emergency off: Operators can flip off a single tenant.
   - Automatic rollback: Triggered by guardrail alerts (see telemetry section).
   - Audit log + change id: All changes include author, change_id, and reason.

Feature switch schema (recommended canonical fields)
- The service storing switches should use the following JSON schema (example):

JSON schema example:
{
  "id": "string (unique)",
  "name": "human-readable string",
  "scope": "global | tenant | cohort",
  "default": "on | off",
  "tenant_overrides": [{"tenant_id": "string", "state": "on | off", "note": "string"}],
  "rollout": {"strategy": "percent | whitelist | gradual", "percent": "0-100", "whitelist": ["tenant_id"], "step_seconds": 3600},
  "metrics": ["list of telemetry keys to evaluate"],
  "auto_rollback": {"enabled": true, "conditions": ["expression strings"]},
  "owner": "team/email",
  "created_by": "user",
  "change_id": "uuid",
  "last_modified": "ISO8601"
}

Integration examples
1) API (control plane)\- Endpoint: POST /api/v1/feature-switches/{id}/apply
   - Example curl to enable for tenant t-123:
     curl -X POST https://feature-switch.redwood.internal/api/v1/feature-switches/llm-prefetch/apply \
       -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' \
       -d '{"tenant_id":"t-123","state":"on","note":"canary for tenant t-123"}'

2) SDK snippet (Node.js)
   - Purpose: Local evaluation to short-circuit expensive controls at request time.
   const flags = await flagsClient.getForTenant(tenantId, ['llm-prefetch']);
   if (flags['llm-prefetch'] === 'on') {
     // call new path
   }

3) Gate at the routing layer (example architecture)
   - Client -> Edge -> Router -> Inference-runtime
   - Router performs a lightweight feature-check (cache first, then control-plane fallback) and attaches X-Feature-Flags header for downstream deterministic behavior.

Caching and TTLs
- Cache tenant flags at edge with a short TTL (default 30s).
- Control-plane changes propagate via event bus (kafka) for near realtime invalidation.
- Use ETag/Version headers in responses from the flags service.

Telemetry and dashboards (concrete recipes)
- Emit these per-tenant metrics from the serving runtime and router: 
  - platform.feature_flags.active{feature="llm-prefetch", tenant_id="t-123"} = 1/0
  - platform.requests.count{tenant_id="t-123", route="chat"}
  - platform.latency.p50_ms{tenant_id="t-123"}
  - platform.latency.p95_ms{tenant_id="t-123"}
  - platform.cost.per_token{tenant_id="t-123"}
  - llm.quality.eval_score{tenant_id="t-123", eval_set="smoke"}

Dashboard panels to create (Prometheus + Grafana)
- Per-feature overview: total tenants with feature on, rollouts in progress, last change_id, owner.
- Risk heatmap: top 20 tenants by request volume with feature on + delta in p95 latency vs baseline.
- KPI gate panels: SLO burn rate, error rate, and quality delta for the last 30m/1h windows.

Alert recipes (Prometheus alert expressions)
- Urgent: Feature-induced latency SLO breach (10m window)
  - alert: FeatureRolloutLatencyBurn
    expr: increase(platform.slo_burn[10m]) > 0.05 and sum by (feature) (increase(platform.requests[10m])) > 100
    for: 5m
    labels: {severity: "critical", team: "platform"}
    annotations: {runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/emergency-model-swap-and-token-surge-mitigation-2026"}

- Quality regression: Eval score drop greater than 5% for the feature cohort versus baseline
  - alert: FeatureQualityRegression
    expr: (avg(llm.quality.eval_score{feature_on="true", window="1h"}) / avg(llm.quality.eval_score{feature_on="false", window="1h"})) < 0.95
    for: 30m
    labels: {severity: "high"}

Automatic rollback criteria (policy examples)
- If p95 latency increases by >30% for >= 5% of requests over a 20-minute window AND absolute SLO burn > 5% in 15m, then: trigger auto_rollback.
- If eval_score drops > 7% on the smoke eval set for >= 2 consecutive evaluation runs, trigger auto_rollback.

Rollback orchestration (operator-safe sequence)
1) Detection: Alert fires or metric threshold crossed.
2) Pause rollout: Feature control-plane action: set rollout.percent = current_percent and freeze.
3) Notify stakeholders via slack channel #platform-rollouts and create incident with change_id.
4) Execute tenant-level rollback for impacted tenants (script example below).

Rollback script (example CLI)
- A: Global kill (fastest):
  curl -X POST https://feature-switch.redwood.internal/api/v1/feature-switches/llm-prefetch/kill \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' \
    -d '{"reason":"auto rollback triggered - latency burn"}'

- B: Per-tenant rollback (selective):
  curl -X POST https://feature-switch.redwood.internal/api/v1/feature-switches/llm-prefetch/apply \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' \
    -d '{"tenant_id":"t-123","state":"off","note":"rollback: latency spike"}'

Runbook: Operator steps (short version)
1) Triage: Check dashboards — feature panels, heatmap, and per-tenant p95 deltas.
2) Scope: Run the SQL to list top impacted tenants:
   SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as requests, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p95_ms
   FROM request_events
   WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '20 minutes' AND feature_flags->>'llm-prefetch' = 'on'
   GROUP BY tenant_id
   ORDER BY requests DESC
   LIMIT 50;
3) If >= 3 high-volume tenants show p95 delta > 30%: pause rollout and issue global kill.
4) For single-tenant regressions: flip per-tenant flag to off and monitor for 30 minutes.
5) After rollback: tag change_id with incident id and complete postmortem template.

Post-rollout retrospective checklist (to be completed within 72h)
- Summary: owner, change_id, start/end times, tenant list impacted.
- Metrics: aggregate p95 delta, SLO burn percent, cost delta.
- Root cause hypothesis: configuration error / runtime regression / model variant mismatch / infra degradation.
- Action items: short-term (fix/rollback), medium-term (add telemetry or gate), long-term (automation).
- Acceptance criteria for re-rollout: explicit KPI gates and a re-run of smoke evals.

Access control and governance
- Only platform ops + product owners may set global-level kill switches.
- Tenant-level overrides allowed for SRE and assigned customer success engineers via scoped RBAC.
- All changes to feature switches must create an audit record retained for 1 year.

Security and secrets
- Control-plane API tokens for programmatic rollouts live in the ops vault.
- Use short-lived tokens for CI-driven rollouts and require MFA for manual global kills.

Operational telemetry retention and cost considerations
- High-cardinality per-tenant metrics are expensive: sample heavy tenants (top 10% by traffic) at full granularity; aggregate lower-volume tenants daily.
- Store daily rollup metrics for 90 days and high-resolution (1m) for 30 days.

Testing and preflight guidance
1) Unit test: flagsClient behavior for on/off/partial percent.
2) Integration test: router and edge cache invalidation with control-plane change propagation tests.
3) Synthetic canary traffic: run 10k synthetic requests per minute for 30 minutes under the feature flag in a staging environment.
4) Degradation simulation: use the platform synthetic-degradation-lab (link below) to validate rollback triggers.

Roadmap and next improvements (owner: eng-platform)
- Q2 2026: Automated KPI gating engine (alpha) that advances rollouts on SLOs.
- Q3 2026: Tenant risk scoring and automated whitelist suggestions.
- Q4 2026: Self-service UI for product teams with RBAC and audit-first workflows.
- 2027: ML-assisted rollback predictor (predicts likely regressions before ramp).

Owners and contacts
- Platform feature-flags service: team-platform-flags@redwood.com (owner: Marcus Huang)
- Platform observability: team-platform-observability@redwood.com (owner: Priya Nair)
- Oncall escalation: #platform-oncall in Slack.

Appendix: Useful queries and commands
- List tenants with feature on and recent p95 delta > 20% (Postgres example):
  WITH recent AS (
    SELECT tenant_id, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p95_ms
    FROM request_events
    WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '30 minutes' AND feature_flags->>'llm-prefetch' = 'on'
    GROUP BY tenant_id
  ), baseline AS (
    SELECT tenant_id, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p95_base
    FROM request_events
    WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '7 days' AND feature_flags->>'llm-prefetch' = 'off'
    GROUP BY tenant_id
  )
  SELECT r.tenant_id, r.p95_ms, b.p95_base, (r.p95_ms / nullif(b.p95_base,0)) - 1 as p95_delta
  FROM recent r JOIN baseline b USING (tenant_id)
  WHERE (r.p95_ms / nullif(b.p95_base,0)) - 1 > 0.20
  ORDER BY p95_delta DESC
  LIMIT 50;

- Quick kill (CLI):
  ./ops-cli feature kill --id llm-prefetch --reason "auto-rollback - latency burn"

References
- /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/emergency-model-swap-and-token-surge-mitigation-2026
- /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/llm-quality-regression-alerting-and-dashboard-guidelines-2026

Document maintenance
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any major incident involving feature flags.
- Owner for reviews: team-platform-flags@redwood.com
